title: Nothing tells a host that a new build needs an explicit, coordinated store cutover
outcome: A host running several projects learns before upgrading that a build changing a rebuildable projection requires an explicit repair per store and a restart of every consumer of that store, instead of discovering it as a mid-work blocker on one project while another project works normally
acceptance: It names who must quiesce and restart long-lived consumers before the repair, and that unrepaired stores keep serving their older consumer until then

The host checklist states that installing a build does not make an existing store usable, names the explicit repair step per store, and says when that step is one-way: after a repair that changes the store's schema, older builds refuse the store and the pre-repair backup restored with the old build is the rollback, while a repair that only re-derives a projection under the same schema leaves the store readable by older builds.

completion.summary: Landed per-store upgrade/cutover guidance in docs/host-checklist.md, including explicit repair/migration classification, coordinated consumer quiescence/restart, interim old-build routing, semantic read-back, and backup rollback. Both revision4 acceptance criteria independently passed on exact gated/reviewed cb7 input; no Medium+ outstanding. Deferred Lows tracked as db47 and0a9f.
